original_question: Over IΣ_n+1 together with WPHP(Σ_n+1), does FRT^2_2(Σ_n+1) follow? Here WPHP(Σ_n+1) says there is no injective Σ_n+1 map F : 2x -> x for some positive x, and FRT^e_k(Σ_n+1) says that for any x there is a y such that every Σ_n+1 coloring C : [y]^e -> k has a homogeneous set H with |H| >= x.
target_in_paper: The draft does not match arXiv:2507.03972, which is a different paper. It matches the first open question in §7 (Questions) of Wei Wang, Finite Combinatorics and Fragments of Arithmetic (arXiv:2506.17943): whether, over IΣ_n, WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) implies FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}).
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right implication direction, namely the open converse from Weak Pigeonhole Principle to a finite Ramsey principle for pairs; it also correctly uses the Σ_{n+1}-definability level and the 2-color/pairs instance FRT^2_2 that the paper singles out as the natural next unresolved case.
missing_details: The base theory in the paper is IΣ_n, not IΣ_{n+1}.
The paper treats n as a fixed positive integer; that external quantification should be stated.
The official target is an open question in §7, not a proved theorem or numbered conjecture in the accessible version of the paper.
WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) is universal in x: for every positive x, there is no injective Σ_{n+1}-definable map F: 2x → x. Your wording 'for some positive x' is not the paper's statement.
FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}) should be stated as a first-order sentence over arithmetic: for every x there exists y such that every Σ_{n+1}-definable coloring C: [y]^2 → 2 has a homogeneous set H of size x.
The paper's official phrasing is 'of size x' rather than '|H| >= x' (though these are interchangeable once one already has a larger homogeneous set).
You should specify that y denotes the initial segment {0, ..., y-1}, and [y]^2 is the set of 2-element subsets of that initial segment.
Homogeneous means that C is constant on [H]^2.
The maps/colorings are definable in the language of first-order arithmetic, as set up in §2.

Nearby in §2-§3 the paper also introduces fairFRT and proves equivalences only for the e = 1 case, so the refined question should explicitly stay with ordinary FRT^2_2 and not drift to those neighboring variants.
The arXiv identifier in the prompt is wrong for this draft; the matching paper is arXiv:2506.17943.
refined_question: Fix a positive integer n. In the language of first-order arithmetic, does IΣ_n prove WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) → FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1})? Here WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) asserts that for every x > 0 there is no injective Σ_{n+1}-definable map F: 2x → x, and FRT^2_2(Σ_{n+1}) asserts that for every x there exists y such that every Σ_{n+1}-definable 2-coloring C: [y]^2 → 2 has a homogeneous set H ⊆ y with |H| = x.
justification: The paper's exact nearby target is the first open question in §7. Section 2 gives the formal meanings of WPHP(Σ_{n+1}) and FRT^e_k(Σ_{n+1}), while §3 shows that only the one-dimensional Ramsey principles collapse to GPHP (Theorem 3.3), so the pairs case FRT^2_2 is the first genuinely unsettled Ramsey instance in this framework. Section 5 proves the opposite implication fails, namely FRT(Σ_{n+1}) does not imply WPHP(Σ_{n+1}), which is precisely the neighboring result that motivates asking for the converse direction instead. Because the accessible paper version does not contain the Conjecture 1.1 / Proposition 1.2 / Theorem 1.3 labels mentioned in the prompt, the closest paper-faithful formulation is the §7 open question, stated over IΣ_n with the §2 definitions.
